papers.authors: Fornazari GA, Montiani-Ferreira F, de Barros Filho IR, Somma AT, Moore B
papers.title: The eye of the Barbary sheep or aoudad (Ammotragus lervia): reference values for selected ophthalmic diagnostic tests, morphologic and biometric observations
papers.why: The only species-level eye study of the aoudad found; its abstract says only 'large and laterally positioned', so the full text may give pupil shape, tapetum and fundus.

papers.authors: Seiko T, Kishida T, Toyama M, Hariyama T, Okitsu T, Wada A, Toda M, Satta Y, Terai Y
papers.title: Visual adaptation of opsin genes to the aquatic environment in sea snakes
papers.why: Open-access article with LWS and RH1 lambda-max values (measured and predicted) for one terrestrial, three amphibious and four aquatic elapids; the abstract does not name the amphibious species (kraits, Laticauda) and the values sit in Fig. 3, which would not open here. Opsin-based, so grade g at most.
papers.species: Laticauda colubrina; Laticauda laticaudata; Laticauda semifasciata

papers.title: Retinal photoreceptors of paleognathous birds: the ostrich (Struthio camelus) and rhea (Rhea americana)
papers.why: Published version of the thesis logged here for Rhea (lambda max pooled with the ostrich in the thesis abstract). It would give the rhea-only cone peaks, including whether the short-wave cone is violet or ultraviolet sensitive, which sets the spectral range.

papers.species: Amegilla albigena; Amegilla andrewsi; Amegilla asserta; Amegilla bombiformis

papers.species: Dipodomys agilis; Dipodomys californicus; Dipodomys compactus; Dipodomys ordii

papers.title: Light perception in two strictly subterranean rodents: life in the dark or blue?
papers.why: Light-choice trials on the silvery mole-rat (Heliophobius argenteocinereus); the abstract infers short-wavelength sensitivity, the full text may give the tested wavelengths and a basis for colour or receptor class. Only the abstract could be read.

papers.authors: West RW, Dowling JE
papers.title: Anatomical evidence for cone and rod-like receptors in the gray squirrel, ground squirrel, and prairie dog retinas
papers.why: Retinal anatomy of the prairie dog, cited by Jacobs et al 1985; gives the receptor types (cones and rod-like receptors) and may give cone classes, closing receptor_classes for Cynomys; its companion Green and Dowling 1975 (J Comp Neurol 159:461-472) gives the electrophysiology.

The fetched page did not show the table values for P. opaca, so the genus value that could stand for P. lineata (rule 3, genus) is not yet logged.
